extracted.intended_audience: DHS/CBP officials, privacy officers, legal practitioners, exporters, and members of the public interested in Privacy Act exemptions and SORN rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: Privacy Act exemption rulemaking for DHS CBP EIS
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending 6 CFR part 5 to exempt portions of the DHS/CBP-020 Export Information System (EIS) from specified Privacy Act provisions, explaining scope, justification, and limited exceptions for those exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemwide exemption claim for DHS/CBP-020 (EIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Homeland Security has exempted the DHS/CBP-020 Export Information System (EIS) from specified provisions of the Privacy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically exempts subsections 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(3); (e)(8); and (g)(1). The rule explains the system consists of electronic and paper records used to collect and process export information (which contains PII) to comply with export laws and facilitate legitimate international trade; CBP enforces export laws at the border and the exporting community must report export data to CBP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for records created during background check and vetting (5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Records created during the background check and vetting process are exempt from the Privacy Act provision 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(3) pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separate statutory basis (k)(2) is asserted for background-check/ vetting records to the extent they would otherwise be covered by the accounting-for-disclosures requirement under (c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: No exemption for travel-related submissions and determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: No exemption will be asserted with respect to information maintained in the system as it relates to data submitted by or on behalf of a person who travels from the United States and crosses the border, nor with respect to the resulting determination (approval or denial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit carve-out: travel-related data and the resulting determinations are not covered by the exemptions claimed in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary may waive exemptions in appropriate circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: After conferring with the appropriate component or agency, DHS may waive applicable exemptions in appropriate circumstances where it would not appear to interfere with or adversely affect the law enforcement purposes of the systems from which the information is recompiled or in which it is contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is discretionary and limited to circumstances where releasing the information would not impede law enforcement, intelligence-related, or national security purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for exemption from 5 U.S.C. 552a(c)(3) — Accounting for Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption from subsection (c)(3) is justified because making available to a record subject the accounting of disclosures would specifically reveal investigative interest in the individual and could reasonably be expected to compromise ongoing investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained harms include: alerting a subject that they are under investigation (including terrorism investigations), enabling destruction of evidence, intimidating witnesses, or allowing a subject to flee to avoid or impede investigation. Exemption is thus warranted on a case-by-case basis when information may impede law enforcement, intelligence, or national security investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for exemption from 5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(8) — Notice on Individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption from subsection (e)(8) is justified because requiring individual notice of disclosure of information due to compulsory legal process would pose an impossible administrative burden and could alert subjects to counterterrorism or law enforcement investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule states notice could reveal investigations not previously known and thereby jeopardize investigative efforts; administrative burden across DHS and other agencies is also cited as a justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for exemption from 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1) — Civil Remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption from subsection (g)(1) is claimed to the extent the system is exempt from other specific subsections of the Privacy Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule ties the civil remedies exemption to the other exemptions asserted (e.g., c(3), e(8)) and limits (g)(1) coverage accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose of EIS as justification for exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP uses EIS to collect and process information to comply with export laws and facilitate legitimate international trade; the system contains personally identifiable information (PII) required of the exporting community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because EIS supports enforcement of U.S. export laws at the border and may be involved in criminal, civil, and administrative enforcement activities, exemptions are justified where disclosure would impede those enforcement or national security objectives.
